tools.title: EPIC motion scores and first 30 days
tools.description: Helps you decide which go to market motion to lead with and what to do first. You give your main GTM challenge, plus your stage and industry and the optional ACV, deal cycle, NRR, TAM, self serve, deal source and geography for a full score. You get a score from 1 to 10 for each of the four EPIC motions from the documented rubric, the primary and secondary motion and the first 30 days of steps for the primary motion, with sector notes when your inputs name the sector. Without the optional inputs the result is marked preliminary.

acv_usd.description: Optional. Average contract value per year in US dollars (for example 42000)

deal_cycle_days.description: Optional. Days from first touch to closed-won (for example 120)

nrr_percent.description: Optional. Net revenue retention in percent (for example 108)

tam_accounts.description: Optional. Number of addressable accounts (for example 2500)

self_serve.description: Optional. true if customers can sign up and get value without talking to sales

deal_source.description: Optional. Where the majority of deals come from

current_channels.description: Optional. What you do today (content, outbound, events, partnerships, PLG, community)

business_model.description: Optional. How you charge: software subscription, services, connectivity, per transaction, marketplace, hardware plus software, or investment management. Read from your other inputs when left out

tools.description: Helps you decide what to do in the next 30, 60 or 90 days for one motion. You give the EPIC motion (E Ecosystem and ABM, P Product-Led Growth, I Inbound and Outbound, C Community-Led) and the time frame. You get immediate, short term and medium term steps, without the self serve steps when your business model is not a software subscription. It builds text from your inputs only.

content.text:
**Consultation:** GTM Alpha Free EPIC audit
Company: Test offer
Challenge: We sell payment processing software. Choose an acquisition test before hiring.

Primary Focus: Ecosystem and ABM
Secondary Focus: Community-Led
EPIC Scores (1 to 10): E:7, P:5, I:6, C:6
Note: Your scores are evenly distributed. This usually means no motion has pulled ahead yet. Pick one motion to test for 90 days with 60% of your GTM effort (Example figure: replace with your own). Measure pipeline contribution, then score again after a quarter to see whether that motion pulls ahead.
Preliminary: rerun when you have ACV, deal cycle, NRR, TAM, deal source, geography.

First 30 days for Ecosystem and ABM:
- Ask a potential referral partner and the buyer to confirm the service problem, introduction owner and approval route.
- Have the delivery lead estimate staff hours and available capacity for the first engagement; finance checks the fee against that cost.
- Agree the buyer acceptance check, accountable service owner and review date before promising a start.

Sector (read from your inputs): fintech. Role check: the founder should ask the current buyer who approves this decision and record the answer before the next planning meeting. The sector committee is a hypothesis to verify: The CFO signs; the Finance Controller or the head of the affected finance team champions; internal audit and compliance review controls; IT checks ERP integration and security; HR joins when employees are affected.

## EPIC rubric scores

**Ecosystem led growth:** 7

**Product led growth:** 5

**Inbound and outbound:** 6

**Community led growth:** 6

**First motion to test:** Ecosystem and ABM

**Secondary focus:** Community-Led

## First month

Ask a potential referral partner and the buyer to confirm the service problem, introduction owner and approval route.

Have the delivery lead estimate staff hours and available capacity for the first engagement; finance checks the fee against that cost.

Agree the buyer acceptance check, accountable service owner and review date before promising a start.

## Sector hypotheses to check

**Sector:** fintech

**Buying roles to confirm:** Owner: founder. Before the next planning meeting, ask the buyer who approves Test offer. Check the authority and approval steps against the buyer's stated process. Candidate roles, not confirmed facts: The CFO signs; the Finance Controller or the head of the affected finance team champions; internal audit and compliance review controls; IT checks ERP integration and security; HR joins when employees are affected.

### Possible measures

days to close the books

reconciliation effort

policy breach rate

approval cycle time

audit findings

cost per transaction

payment success rate

### Questions to validate

Our ERP already does this

Security and compliance review

Migration will disrupt the close

Regulatory caution

**Evidence to collect:** Close time or reconciliation effort before and after for one entity, signed off by the finance controller.

**Proposed sales motion:** CFO-led with a security and compliance review inside the cycle; proof through a pilot on one entity or department.

**Business model:** services (people-delivered, per FTE, per ticket or fixed price)

## Epic detail

### Rubric scores

**Ecosystem led growth:** 7

**Product led growth:** 5

**Inbound and outbound:** 6

**Community led growth:** 6

**First motion to test:** E

**Suggested motion:** Ecosystem and ABM

**Method:** EPIC motion scoring, advanced version (epic-motion-diagnostic rubric, Helix GTM Consulting)

**Scale:** 1 to 10 per motion

### Primary

**Letter:** E

**Motion:** Ecosystem and ABM

**Reason:** Ecosystem and ABM scores 7 of 10: Series B starting point 7; no further adjustment changed it.

### Secondary

**Letter:** C

**Motion:** Community-Led

**Reason:** Community-Led scores 6 of 10: Series B starting point 6; no further adjustment changed it.

### Warnings



### Limits and assumptions

Your scores are evenly distributed. This usually means no motion has pulled ahead yet. Pick one motion to test for 90 days with 60% of your GTM effort (Example figure: replace with your own). Measure pipeline contribution, then score again after a quarter to see whether that motion pulls ahead.

**Preliminary:** true

### Skipped adjustments

ACV

deal cycle

NRR

TAM

deal source

geography

**Evidence limit:** Preliminary: rerun when you have ACV, deal cycle, NRR, TAM, deal source, geography.

**Stage used:** Series B

### Adjustments applied

**Rule:** Stage starting point: Series B

#### Change

**Ecosystem led growth:** 7

**Product led growth:** 5

**Inbound and outbound:** 6

**Community led growth:** 6

## Reading the answer

For Test offer, the rubric supports a first test of Ecosystem and ABM. It does not establish that hiring another sales team will pay back. Acquisition cost, buyer acceptance and delivery capacity need direct evidence. The conclusion needs review if a comparable buyer cannot complete the proposed first step, delivery misses acceptance, or measured acquisition and delivery costs exceed the agreed budget.

## Decisions by role

Proposed owners. Confirm the named person before acting.

Founder: ask a buyer to test the assumption behind "We sell payment processing software. Choose an acquisition test before hiring." before endorsing Ecosystem and ABM; record the buyer observation that would reverse the choice.

CEO: have finance and the delivery lead cost a small Ecosystem and ABM test for Test offer before adding staff; agree a spending limit and stop if accepted work cannot cover acquisition and delivery cost.

CMO: separate the supplied channel description "the stated acquisition channels" from measured results; check source, period and buyer acceptance before claiming the channel works.

CRO: compare the supplied annual value of USD not stated and unstated day cycle with closed and lost deals before expanding Ecosystem and ABM; record scope and cycle differences.

Demand generation head: choose a small, dated account sample from the unstated number of addressable accounts; record reach, qualified conversations and acquisition effort before widening Ecosystem and ABM.

content.text:
**Timeframe:** 90-day

**First motion to test:** Ecosystem and ABM

## Schedule

**Immediate:** Days 1 to 30

**Short term:** Days 31 to 60

**Medium term:** Days 61 to 90

## Proposed actions

### Immediate

Ask a potential referral partner and the buyer to confirm the service problem, introduction owner and approval route.

Have the delivery lead estimate staff hours and available capacity for the first engagement; finance checks the fee against that cost.

Agree the buyer acceptance check, accountable service owner and review date before promising a start.

### Short term

Run the agreed service engagement within the confirmed staffing and scope; record actual hours, exceptions and rework.

Ask the buyer to accept or reject the deliverable using the agreed evidence; record unresolved concerns.

Compare the actual acquisition and delivery cost with the agreed fee before accepting more work.

### Medium term

Repeat the engagement only if the buyer acceptance and margin checks pass; otherwise revise scope, fee or delivery method.

Ask the delivery lead to confirm spare capacity before widening the account or referral list.

Review buyer outcomes and repeat purchase intent before adding a sales team; dates remain proposed until owners agree.

**Business model:** services (people-delivered, per FTE, per ticket or fixed price)

## Reading the answer

This 90 day partner and account sequence supports planning a bounded service engagement. Team capacity, budget and an agreed start are not supplied by this tool. Treat dates and example account counts as proposals. Review the conclusion if the buyer rejects the acceptance check or acquisition and delivery costs exceed the agreed resource limit.

## Decisions by role

Proposed owners. Confirm the named person before acting.

Founder: ask a buyer to agree the outcome and exclusions for the service engagement before accepting the partner and account sequence; record what would make them reject it.

CEO: have the delivery lead cost the service engagement against available staff time before approving the 90 day schedule; reduce scope if capacity is insufficient.

CMO: check the claim used in the partner and account approach against the accepted service engagement evidence before publishing it; keep unmeasured benefits labelled as hypotheses.

CRO: ask the buyer to confirm an approver, acceptance check and feasible start for the service engagement before treating the 90 day dates as mutual commitments.

Demand generation head: cap the partner and account outreach sample at the team's confirmed follow up capacity; compare accepted engagements and acquisition effort before increasing volume.
